note: Mitarai et al., Quantum circuit learning. Simulation only: "we show by simulation that a 6-qubit circuit is capable of fitting dynamics of 3 spins out of a 10-spin system". No device, no vendor, no compute description, no availability statement anywhere in 16 chunks. qubit_count 6 is the circuit they simulated.

Zuchongzhi, 66 functional qubits (device capacity; the sampling task used 56). quantum_vendor not_reported: built at USTC, but the parsed text carries numbered affiliation markers without institution strings, and gold records what the paper states. HALLUCINATION TRAP on the GPU fields -- the only GPUs named are Summit's 27,648, invoked hypothetically to price a classical simulation. The authors' own machine was "a single node server that has 1536 GB memory and four CPUs (Intel-Xeon-Gold-6254)". A system reporting a GPU here is inventing one.

LAWS. PennyLane 0.22.2 simulation, no device. "We release our source code implemented by Pennylane at https://github.com/taozeyi1990/LAWS". dataset_access open: "The classification training data is public and can be downloaded from the PennyLane tutorial." qubit_count LEFT NULL -- "large system sizes (40 qubits)" and a 3-qubit figure circuit both appear, and I cannot tell from the passages which is theirs. DECIDE.

Benedetti et al., review of parameterized quantum circuits as ML models. No experiments of its own. quantum_vendor IBM is authored; device_name LEFT NULL because it is blocked on the same unresolved question -- if a survey's cited hardware counts, this needs "IBM Q5 Yorktown" and "IBM Q5 Tenerife" and the field is singular; if it does not, quantum_vendor should be not_reported. code_url not_reported: Table III surveys other people's open-source software.

Regularizing quantum loss landscapes by noise injection. "We perform numerical experiments for up to n = 10 qubits". code_url not_reported although the paper does claim code exists: "Our code is available at [37]" resolves to a bibliography entry, so no URL appears in the body. This is the cleanest test in the set of whether the extractor invents a URL from an availability claim.

Virtual distillation. Theory throughout: N is the number of qubits per system and M the number of copies, both symbolic. The "six-qubit circuit" is a figure illustrating the construction, not an experiment. 133 qubit-mentions and not one reports a run -- the strongest not_reported case in the set.

Synergetic QEM by randomized compiling and ZNE. "The experimental curves are generated by classical simulation of a VQE algorithm on a noisy quantum computer" -- simulated, no device. Software named (True-Q, SciPy, BOBYQA, OpenFermion) but no repository and no availability statement anywhere in 29 chunks. qubit_count not_reported: every count is symbolic (n-qubit Pauli operators), MODERATE confidence -- a molecule size may sit in a table.

TNQVM/ExaTN simulator. quantum_vendor not_reported -- IBM appears only as a cloud provider whose noise models the framework *can* query, a capability claim. qubit_count 53: they simulate Sycamore random circuits at 53 qubits. SCHEMA LIMIT on the GPU fields: the benchmark table has four configurations (DGX-A100 with 8 A100; DGX-1 with 8 V100; 16 nodes / 96 V100; 64 nodes / 384 V100). A single-valued field cannot hold that. I recorded the largest, which will score a system reporting "8 A100" as wrong. device_name "NVIDIA and AMD GPU" is authored, and by the convention above a GPU is not a device_name -- DECIDE.

Google Sycamore QAOA on non-planar graphs. "The code used in this experiment is available at https://github.com/quantumlib/ReCirq"; "The experimental data for this experiment is available on Figshare". CONTRADICTION with the authored qubit_count 23: 23 is the qubits used ("restricted to 23 physical qubits"), but the paper also states Sycamore "consists of a two-dimensional array of 54 transmon qubits". Under the device-capacity convention this is 54. The Zuchongzhi record uses device capacity (66, not the 56 used). One of the two must move.

ML-based surface code decoding. Classical ML over simulated syndromes; the qubit counts are textbook exposition of distance-d surface codes, not a run. "Data from the numerical simulations and the code can be made available upon reasonable request" -- code_url not_reported because no URL is given, dataset_access "on request". VOCABULARY GAP: the schema hint says open|licensed|irb|none and none of those fits a request-only policy.

Tensor-network simulation on modern GPUs. "Our experimental work was carried out on a DGX-A100 equipped with eight NVIDIA A100-SXM-80GB GPUs." qubit_count 53 from the 53-qubit Sycamore circuits they verify. HALLUCINATION TRAP: Sycamore is named throughout, but as the circuits being *simulated* -- no quantum hardware was used, so quantum_vendor and device_name are not_reported. Best single test in the set of whether the extractor distinguishes simulating a device from running on one.

SQD-enabled circuit compression. "circuits are transpiled to the ibm_rensselaer instruction set ... and sampled with 100k shots via IBM Qiskit SamplerV2"; "on ibm_rensselaer (Eagle r3, 127 qubits)". qubit_count 127 is device capacity; the experiments used 3-6 contextual-subspace qubits, so this is the same capacity-vs-used fork as Zuchongzhi and Sycamore. dataset_access not_reported: the 21 molecules are generated with PySCF, not distributed.

QAOA-GPT. No quantum hardware: circuits are "ready to be simulated classically or transpiled to be run on a quantum device" -- future tense. "For the GPT model training, we use a single NVIDIA A100 GPU node" and "NVIDIA A100 GPUs on NERSC's Perlmutter"; gpu_count 4 is the largest configuration reported ("distributing the gradient evaluation across four GPUs"). AMBIGUOUS: "a single A100 GPU node" may itself be 4 or 8 GPUs. dataset_access open: "source code and computational results are available at" the repository.

Hybrid quantum-classical sampling for discrete MRFs. qubit_count 40 -- the largest chain simulated ("at n = 40, chi = 32 achieves F = 0.721"). quantum_vendor not_reported and device_name "BlueQubit" is authored: BlueQubit is a simulator platform (bluequbit_sv / bluequbit_mps backends), and the paper says outright that cloud execution was abandoned as queue-bound and all reported timings are "MEASURED ON THE SAME LOCAL CPU". By the convention above this is not a device_name -- DECIDE, together with the TNQVM "NVIDIA and AMD GPU" record.

Sivak, Newman, Klimov (Google Quantum AI), Optimization of Decoder Priors. "repetition and surface code memory experiments executed on Google's Sycamore processor". qubit_count not_reported: this paper never states Sycamore's capacity, only code distances (d=21 repetition, d=3,5 surface) -- a real case of a named device with no stated qubit count. dataset_access not_reported: the QEC datasets are cited to reference [22], not offered. Newman, Modularity and community structure in networks (2006). Hardware fields already authored not_reported. No repository (pre-dates the practice) and no availability statement: network data is credited in the acknowledgements ("thank ... for providing network data"), which is attribution, not access.

CORPUS DEFECT -- DO NOT AUTHOR. The stored PDF is an OSTI.GOV landing page, not the paper: 4 chunks, all of them search-portal chrome, citation-export widgets and the abstract. There is no paper text to read, so every field must stay null. not_reported would be wrong -- it asserts the paper is silent, when in fact we never obtained the paper, and scoring it would charge a parse failure to the extractor. Re-fetch from the DOI (10.1109/QCE52317.2021.00032) or drop it.

Newman & Girvan, Finding and evaluating community structure (2004). Hardware fields already authored not_reported. Same reasoning as the other Newman paper: no repository, and the only data language is an acknowledgement of useful comments.

Hamming 1950. Mentions Bell Labs Model 5 Relay Computers -- hardware, but not a field this schema has. A useful reminder that not_reported means 'this schema's field is absent from the paper', not 'the paper describes no hardware'. Confident across the board.

Hamiltonian-Informed Point Group Symmetry-Respecting Ansatz for VQE. MindSpore Quantum simulation, explicitly noiseless: "all simulations in this study are conducted under idealized conditions where both sampling noise and hardware-induced noise are neglected" -- so no device. qubit_count 28 is the largest in Table I (C2H4); the table spans 12-28. "The code and data supporting this study are publicly available at" the atomgit URL (the underscores in `paper_with_code` were spaces in the PDF text layer).
